strict clock, yule tree prior root_age 6.00 7.038 4.143 10.622 863 pass
strict clock, yule tree prior clock_rate 0.15 0.131 0.094 0.162 404 pass
strict clock, coalescent tree prior root_age 6.00 11.727 4.386 25.400 1026 info-pass
strict clock, coalescent tree prior clock_rate 0.15 0.134 0.105 0.170 199 info-pass

Under the coalescent prior the root moves from 7.0 to 11.7 ky (posterior means), with an upper HPD limit of 25 ky. The calibrated nodes and the rate hardly change. The uncalibrated root, which is constrained mainly by the tree prior, is where the choice of prior matters.

H.4.11 Multispecies coalescent in a dialect continuum

Script 11_multispecies_coalescent.Rev implements the multispecies coalescent of Section 16.2.1 (Rannala and Yang 2003; Heled and Drummond 2010). The five “species” are languages, each sampled at two local varieties (“individuals”). Eight “loci” are concept blocks, each with 200 binary cognate characters that share one concept tree (gene tree). The concept trees grow inside the language tree under dnMultiSpeciesCoalescent, with incomplete sorting of ancestral lexical variation across the short internal branches. The language-tree topology and ages and the effective population size \(N_e\) are the targets. The clock rate is fixed at its true value, because the absolute time scale and \(N_e\) cannot both be identified without a calibration. Treating a block of characters as one locus with a single history is an idealization: in real lexical data each meaning would be a separate, very short locus. In RevBayes 1.4.1 a pair of lineages coalesces at rate \(2/N_e\) per unit of tree time, so the expected time to coalescence of two lineages is \(N_e/2\) rather than the \(N_e\) implied by the units of Equation (16.1). We verified this by simulating from dnMultiSpeciesCoalescent and by recomputing its log density by hand, and the R simulator uses the same parameterization.

The script has two modes, and the table shows both.

  • genetrees clamps the eight true concept trees. This tests the MSC density and the inference of the language tree and \(N_e\) on their own.
  • joint (the default) estimates the concept trees from the cognate characters together with everything else.

Getting the joint mode to run at all took three changes, and all three are documented in the script.

  1. Runaway towards \(N_e \to 0\). With an exponential prior on \(N_e\), the sampler repeatedly ran away towards \(N_e \to 0\), with log densities above \(10^{60}\). This happened when root-age or subtree-scale proposals produced language trees with negative branch lengths, or concept trees incompatible with the language tree. A clamped “guard” observation now gives zero density to negative species-tree branches, mvSpeciesSubtreeScaleBeta is not used, and \(N_e\) has a Uniform(0.05, 5) prior.
  2. Starting tree. The language tree starts from a data-derived UPGMA tree, because from a random start the joint sampler stayed on a wrong topology.
  3. Mixing. Even with these changes the joint mode mixes poorly in a few minutes. The topology is recovered, but the ages stay near their starting values and their HPDs are far too narrow, so those rows fail. The genetrees mode recovers every parameter. Running the joint model reliably would need much longer chains or better joint species-gene moves.
################################################################################
# 11_multispecies_coalescent.Rev
#
# Model    : multispecies coalescent (Rannala & Yang 2003; Heled & Drummond
#            2010) for a dialect continuum: 5 languages ("species"), each
#            sampled at 2 local varieties ("individuals"); 8 independent
#            concept blocks ("loci"), each with its own concept tree (gene
#            tree) evolving inside the language tree with incomplete lineage
#            sorting of ancestral lexical variation. Each block is a set of
#            binary cognate characters sharing one history (an idealisation:
#            in real lexical data each meaning would be one short "locus").
#            Gene trees ~ dnMultiSpeciesCoalescent(language tree, Ne);
#            characters ~ binary CTMC on the gene trees with a known clock rate.
#            Note: in RevBayes 1.4.1 a pair of lineages coalesces at rate 2/Ne
#            (time units of the tree), i.e. E[pair coalescence time] = Ne/2;
#            data/sim_time.R simulates with the same parameterisation.
# Book     : Ch. 16 "The multispecies coalescent and incomplete lineage
#            sorting" (biology-toolkit-msc)
# Estimates: language (species) tree topology and ages, Ne, 8 concept trees
# Data     : data/time/msc_locus1..8.nex, msc_species_map.tsv, msc_setup.Rev
# Runtime  : ~2-3 min (one run; the MSC likelihood over 8 loci is the costly part)
# Usage    : cd revbayes && rb analyses/time/11_multispecies_coalescent.Rev [--args n_gen MODE]
#            MODE joint (default): concept trees estimated from the characters
#            MODE genetrees: the true concept trees are clamped (tests the MSC
#                 density and the language-tree/Ne inference on their own)
################################################################################

seed(1111)
n_gen = 7000
mode = "joint"
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
if (args.size() > 2) mode = args[3]
out_dir = "output/time/11_multispecies_coalescent/" + mode + "_"

source("data/time/msc_setup.Rev")        # n_loci, msc_clock_rate, species_names
taxa <- readTaxonData("data/time/msc_species_map.tsv")
for (i in 1:species_names.size()) sp_taxa[i] = taxon(species_names[i])
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

#### language (species) tree: Yule prior ######################################
sp_root_age ~ dnUniform(0.1, 20.0)
sp_lambda ~ dnExponential(1.0)
sptree ~ dnBDP(lambda=sp_lambda, mu=0.0, rho=1.0, rootAge=sp_root_age, taxa=sp_taxa)
moves.append( mvScale(sp_lambda, lambda=1.0, tune=true, weight=1.0) )
if (mode != "genetrees") {
  # joint mode: start from a data-derived UPGMA language tree (root 2.5 ky),
  # because the joint sampler cannot escape a wrong starting topology in a
  # few thousand generations (the concept trees adapt to it)
  sp_start <- readTrees("data/time/msc_species_start.tre")[1]
  sp_root_age.setValue(sp_start.rootAge())
  sptree.setValue(sp_start)
}

# Guard against negative species-tree branch lengths. A proposal on the root
# age can put the root below one of its children; with no character data on
# the species tree nothing else rejects such a state, and the MSC density of
# RevBayes 1.4.1 then becomes arbitrarily large (we observed the chain running
# away to Ne -> 0 with log densities > 1e60). The observation below has
# density 1/(min_bl + 1e6), constant to within 1e-6 for any valid tree, and
# zero when a branch is negative.
for (i in 1:(2 * species_names.size() - 2)) sp_bl[i] := sptree.branchLength(i)
sp_min_bl := min(sp_bl)
sp_guard ~ dnUniform(-1e6, sp_min_bl)
sp_guard.clamp(0.0)

#### effective population size (shared by all branches) #######################
# Uniform prior bounded away from 0: with an unbounded prior (Exponential(1))
# the joint sampler ran away to Ne -> 0 with an ever-increasing MSC density in
# RevBayes 1.4.1, even with the branch-length guard above.
Ne ~ dnUniform(0.05, 5.0)
Ne.setValue(1.0)
moves.append( mvScale(Ne, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=5.0) )

#### concept (gene) trees ######################################################
if (mode == "genetrees") {
  # verification of the MSC density alone: the true concept trees are observed
  true_gene_trees <- readTrees("data/time/msc_gene_trees_true.tre")
  for (l in 1:n_loci) {
    gene_tree[l] ~ dnMultiSpeciesCoalescent(speciesTree=sptree, Ne=Ne, taxa=taxa)
    gene_tree[l].clamp(true_gene_trees[l])
  }
} else {
  # full model: concept trees estimated from binary cognate characters
  pi ~ dnDirichlet(v(1, 1))
  Q := fnF81(pi)
  moves.append( mvBetaSimplex(pi, alpha=20, tune=true, weight=2.0) )
  for (l in 1:n_loci) {
    gene_tree[l] ~ dnMultiSpeciesCoalescent(speciesTree=sptree, Ne=Ne, taxa=taxa)
    locus_data[l] <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/time/msc_locus" + l + ".nex")
    seq[l] ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree=gene_tree[l], Q=Q, branchRates=msc_clock_rate, type="Standard")
    seq[l].clamp(locus_data[l])
    moves.append( mvNNI(gene_tree[l], weight=1.0) )
    moves.append( mvNarrow(gene_tree[l], weight=1.0) )
    moves.append( mvFNPR(gene_tree[l], weight=0.5) )
    moves.append( mvNodeTimeSlideUniform(gene_tree[l], weight=2.0) )
    moves.append( mvSubtreeScale(gene_tree[l], weight=0.5) )
    moves.append( mvRootTimeScaleBactrian(gene_tree[l], weight=0.5) )
  }
}

#### species-tree moves ########################################################
# plain moves (gene trees held fixed; valid Metropolis-Hastings proposals)
moves.append( mvSlide(sp_root_age, delta=0.05, tune=true, weight=4.0) )
moves.append( mvNodeTimeSlideUniform(sptree, weight=4.0) )
moves.append( mvNarrow(sptree, weight=2.0) )
moves.append( mvFNPR(sptree, weight=1.0) )
if (mode != "genetrees") {
  # joint moves that also update the gene trees (mvSpeciesSubtreeScaleBeta
  # is not used: it produced the runaway state described above)
  mv_sp_narrow = mvSpeciesNarrow(speciesTree=sptree, weight=4.0)
  mv_sp_slide  = mvSpeciesNodeTimeSlideUniform(speciesTree=sptree, weight=4.0)
  mv_sp_scale  = mvSpeciesTreeScale(speciesTree=sptree, rootAge=sp_root_age, weight=3.0)
  for (l in 1:n_loci) {
    mv_sp_narrow.addGeneTreeVariable(gene_tree[l])
    mv_sp_slide.addGeneTreeVariable(gene_tree[l])
    mv_sp_scale.addGeneTreeVariable(gene_tree[l])
  }
  moves.append( mv_sp_narrow )
  moves.append( mv_sp_slide )
  moves.append( mv_sp_scale )
}

age_AB  := tmrca(sptree, clade("A", "B"))
age_DE  := tmrca(sptree, clade("D", "E"))
age_CDE := tmrca(sptree, clade("C", "D", "E"))

#### MCMC ######################################################################
mymodel = model(sptree)
monitors.append( mnModel(filename=out_dir + "model.log", printgen=5) )
monitors.append( mnFile(sptree, filename=out_dir + "species.trees", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=1000, sp_root_age, Ne, sp_min_bl) )
mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=n_gen, tuningInterval=200)

trace = readTreeTrace(out_dir + "species.trees", treetype="clock", burnin=0.25)
mcc = mccTree(trace, file=out_dir + "species_mcc.tre")

q()

H.4.12 Episodic (skyline) birth-death diversification

Script 12_episodic_birth_death_skyline.Rev fits a piecewise-constant birth-death model (Stadler et al. 2013) to a fixed dated tree of about 100 languages (Section 16.6.1). Language splitting has its own rate in each of three intervals (0 to 1.5, 1.5 to 3 and more than 3 ky ago); language death has one constant rate. The tree is larger than the others in this appendix because rates are estimated from branching times alone. Extinction is held constant to respect the non-identifiability of fully time-varying birth and death rates from trees of living languages (Louca and Pennell 2020). The check asks whether the slowdown of splitting towards the present is detected.

################################################################################
# 12_episodic_birth_death_skyline.Rev
#
# Model    : episodic (piecewise-constant, "skyline") birth-death process on a
#            dated language-family tree (Stadler 2011, 2013): the speciation
#            (language-splitting) rate takes a different value in each of 3
#            time intervals (boundaries 1.5 and 3.0 ky), extinction (language
#            death) rate constant. dnEpisodicBirthDeath, tree fixed (clamped).
#            The tree is larger (about 100 languages) than in the other
#            scripts because diversification rates are estimated from
#            branching times alone. Extinction is held constant across
#            intervals to respect the non-identifiability of fully time-varying
#            lambda and mu from extant trees (Louca & Pennell 2020).
# Book     : Ch. 16 "Diversification models" (biology-toolkit-diversification)
#            and "Phylodynamics" (birth-death skyline)
# Estimates: lambda_1 (0-1.5 ky), lambda_2 (1.5-3 ky), lambda_3 (> 3 ky), mu;
#            posterior probability that splitting slowed towards the present
# Data     : data/time/skyline_tree.nex, skyline_setup.Rev
# Runtime  : < 1 min
# Usage    : cd revbayes && rb analyses/time/12_episodic_birth_death_skyline.Rev [--args n_gen]
################################################################################

seed(1212)
n_gen = 20000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/time/12_episodic_birth_death_skyline/"

source("data/time/skyline_setup.Rev")      # sky_root_age, sky_times
observed_tree <- readTrees("data/time/skyline_tree.nex")[1]
taxa <- observed_tree.taxa()
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

n_int = sky_times.size() + 1
for (i in 1:n_int) {
  speciation[i] ~ dnLognormal(ln(0.5), 1.0)
  moves.append( mvScale(speciation[i], lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=2.0) )
}
extinction ~ dnExponential(5.0)
moves.append( mvScale(extinction, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=2.0) )
ext_vec := rep(extinction, n_int)

timetree ~ dnEpisodicBirthDeath(rootAge=observed_tree.rootAge(), lambdaRates=speciation,
                                lambdaTimes=sky_times, muRates=ext_vec, muTimes=sky_times,
                                rho=1.0, samplingStrategy="uniform", condition="survival",
                                taxa=taxa)
timetree.clamp(observed_tree)

net_div := speciation - ext_vec
slowdown := ifelse(speciation[1] < speciation[n_int], 1, 0)
gamma_stat := observed_tree.gammaStatistic()

mymodel = model(timetree)
monitors.append( mnModel(filename=out_dir + "model.log", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=5000, speciation, extinction) )
mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=n_gen, tuningInterval=200)

q()
Model Parameter Truth Post. mean HPD low HPD high ESS Status

episodic birth-death (3 intervals) lambda_2 (1.5-3 ky) 0.6 0.510 0.275 0.769 719 pass
episodic birth-death (3 intervals) lambda_3 (>3 ky) 1.0 1.216 0.750 1.809 842 pass
episodic birth-death (3 intervals) mu 0.1 0.151 0.000 0.399 719 pass
episodic birth-death (3 intervals) P(lambda_1 < lambda_3) (slowdown) 1.0 1.000 NA NA NA pass

All three splitting rates and the extinction rate are covered, and the slowdown towards the present is detected with posterior probability 1.

H.4.13 State-dependent diversification (BiSSE)

Script 13_bisse_state_dependent_diversification.Rev implements BiSSE (Maddison et al. 2007) with the character-dependent birth-death process dnCDBDP, on a fixed tree of 150 languages simulated by diversitree (FitzJohn 2012) with a binary trait under which state-1 languages split twice as fast. The tree is clamped with clamp and the tip states with clampCharData. check_time.R compares the posterior with the diversitree maximum-likelihood estimates. HiSSE (Beaulieu and O’Meara 2016) uses the same distribution with four states (two observed by two hidden) and ambiguous tip coding, and the character-independent null models it needs are built the same way. We have not run these, because a convincing test of HiSSE needs much larger trees than are practical here. The caution of Rabosky and Goldberg (2015) applies: a single clade with both the trait and a high rate can produce spurious support for state dependence.

All six rates are covered by their 95% HPDs. However, the posterior probability that \(\lambda_1 > \lambda_0\) is only about 0.91, below the 0.95 threshold, so that row is reported as a fail. The diversitree ML estimates show the same weak contrast in this simulated tree (\(\hat\lambda_0 = 0.64\), \(\hat\lambda_1 = 0.78\), against true values 0.4 and 0.8). The shortfall is a property of this simulated data set rather than of the implementation: 150 languages are too few to detect a twofold difference in splitting rate reliably.

################################################################################
# 13_bisse_state_dependent_diversification.Rev
#
# Model    : BiSSE, binary-state speciation and extinction (Maddison et al.
#            2007): languages in state 0 / 1 of a binary trait (e.g. a
#            subsistence mode or a writing tradition) split at rates
#            lambda0 / lambda1 and die at rates mu0 / mu1; the trait changes
#            at rates q01 / q10. dnCDBDP (character-dependent birth-death),
#            tree fixed (clamped), tip states clamped with clampCharData.
#            Uses ~150 languages: SSE models need large trees for power.
#            A HiSSE extension uses the same machinery with 4 states (2
#            observed x 2 hidden) and ambiguous tip coding; it is not run
#            here (see docs/time.Rmd).
# Book     : Ch. 16 "Diversification models" (biology-toolkit-diversification):
#            BiSSE, HiSSE and the Rabosky & Goldberg caution
# Estimates: lambda0, lambda1, mu0, mu1, q01, q10; P(lambda1 > lambda0)
# Data     : data/time/bisse_tree.nex, data/time/bisse_trait.nex
# Runtime  : ~2 min
# Usage    : cd revbayes && rb analyses/time/13_bisse_state_dependent_diversification.Rev [--args n_gen]
################################################################################

seed(1313)
n_gen = 4000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/time/13_bisse_state_dependent_diversification/"

observed_tree <- readTrees("data/time/bisse_tree.nex")[1]
trait <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/time/bisse_trait.nex")
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

n_states = 2
for (i in 1:n_states) {
  speciation[i] ~ dnLognormal(ln(0.5), 1.0)
  extinction[i] ~ dnExponential(5.0)
  moves.append( mvScale(speciation[i], lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=2.0) )
  moves.append( mvScale(extinction[i], lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=2.0) )
}
lambda0 := speciation[1]
lambda1 := speciation[2]
mu0 := extinction[1]
mu1 := extinction[2]
diff_lambda := lambda1 - lambda0
lambda1_gt_lambda0 := ifelse(lambda1 > lambda0, 1, 0)

q01 ~ dnExponential(10.0)
q10 ~ dnExponential(10.0)
moves.append( mvScale(q01, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=1.0) )
moves.append( mvScale(q10, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=1.0) )
rate_matrix := fnFreeK([q01, q10], rescaled=false)

root_freq ~ dnDirichlet(rep(1, n_states))
moves.append( mvBetaSimplex(root_freq, alpha=20, tune=true, weight=1.0) )

timetree ~ dnCDBDP(rootAge=observed_tree.rootAge(), speciationRates=speciation,
                   extinctionRates=extinction, Q=rate_matrix, delta=1.0,
                   pi=root_freq, rho=1.0, condition="time", nTimeSlices=50)
timetree.clamp(observed_tree)
timetree.clampCharData(trait)

mymodel = model(timetree)
monitors.append( mnModel(filename=out_dir + "model.log", printgen=3) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=1000, speciation, extinction) )
mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=n_gen, tuningInterval=200)

q()

H.4.14 Effective priors of calibrated nodes

Script 14_effective_prior_calibrations.Rev puts into practice the advice of Section 10.3.2 to always sample from the prior. It runs the model of script 01 without the cognate data and records the effective (marginal) prior of the two calibrated nodes and the root. For the calibrated nodes, Truth is the mean of the density the analyst specified, so the difference between it and the posterior-mean column measures how much the tree prior and the ordering constraints have shifted the effective prior (Heled and Drummond 2012; Warnock et al. 2012). In RevBayes 1.4.1, run(underPrior=true) reported “no effect” for this model, so the script leaves out the dnPhyloCTMC node. That keeps the calibration densities and drops only the data.

The results illustrate two pitfalls. First, the soft-bounded uniform on C1 (95% of its mass in [0.96, 1.96] ky) becomes an effective prior centred near 1.9 ky, half a millennium older than the analyst specified, because of the Yule prior and the older calibration C2 above it. Second, the effective prior on the uncalibrated root is narrow and young, about 4.3 ky. With the topology free under the prior, the clade C2 (all languages except one) almost always contains the root, so the C2 calibration ends up dating the root itself. Once the data fix the topology, the root is no longer calibrated, and the posterior of script 01 is far wider (4.0 to 10.3 ky). A calibration on a large clade whose monophyly is not enforced can therefore act on a different node from the one intended. The notes column of results_time.csv reports how often this happens.

################################################################################
# 14_effective_prior_calibrations.Rev
#
# Model    : the model of script 01 (Yule prior x calibration densities C1, C2,
#            strict clock, binary CTMC) sampled WITHOUT the data
#            (mcmc(..., underPrior=TRUE)) to obtain the effective (marginal)
#            prior on calibrated and uncalibrated node ages. The book's advice
#            "always sample from the prior": the effective prior on a
#            calibrated node is the product of the calibration density, the
#            tree prior and the ordering constraints, and can differ from the
#            specified density. tests/check_time.R compares it with the
#            specified densities and with the posterior from script 01.
# Book     : Ch. 10 "How calibrations interact" (divergence-interaction)
# Estimates: effective prior of age_C1, age_C2 and the root age
# Data     : taxon names of data/time/clock_strict.nex only
# Runtime  : ~30 s
# Usage    : cd revbayes && rb analyses/time/14_effective_prior_calibrations.Rev [--args n_gen]
################################################################################

seed(1414)
n_gen = 50000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/time/14_effective_prior_calibrations/"

data <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/time/clock_strict.nex")
taxa <- data.taxa()
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

root_age ~ dnUniform(0.5, 30.0)
birth_rate ~ dnExponential(1.0)
timetree ~ dnBDP(lambda=birth_rate, mu=0.0, rho=1.0, rootAge=root_age,
                 samplingStrategy="uniform", condition="time", taxa=taxa)
start_tree <- readTrees("data/time/clock_strict_upgma_start.tre")[1]
root_age.setValue(start_tree.rootAge())
timetree.setValue(start_tree)

moves.append( mvScale(birth_rate, lambda=1.0, tune=true, weight=1.0) )
moves.append( mvSlide(root_age, delta=1.0, tune=true, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvTreeScale(tree=timetree, rootAge=root_age, delta=0.5, tune=true, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvNodeTimeSlideUniform(timetree, weight=10.0) )
moves.append( mvSubtreeScale(timetree, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvNarrow(timetree, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvFNPR(timetree, weight=2.0) )

source("data/time/calibrations_tree12.Rev")
age_C1 := tmrca(timetree, clade_C1)
age_C2 := tmrca(timetree, clade_C2)
obs_C1 ~ dnSoftBoundUniformNormal(min=C1_min - age_C1, max=C1_max - age_C1, sd=C1_sd, p=0.95)
obs_C1.clamp(0.0)
obs_C2 ~ dnLognormal(mean=C2_mu, sd=C2_sd, offset=-age_C2)
obs_C2.clamp(-C2_offset)

# No clock and no dnPhyloCTMC node: the cognate data are not part of this model. (In RevBayes
# 1.4.1 run(underPrior=true) reports "no effect" here; also, clamped
# calibration "observations" count as likelihood terms, so leaving out the
# data node is the clean way to keep the calibrations and drop the data.)

mymodel = model(timetree)
monitors.append( mnModel(filename=out_dir + "model.log", printgen=20) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=10000, root_age, age_C1, age_C2) )
mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=n_gen, tuningInterval=200)

q()

calibrations x Yule prior, no data age_C2 effective prior 4.41 4.301 3.859 4.862 1748 info

H.4.15 Rate variation among meanings biases dates

Script 15_gamma_rate_variation_dating_bias.Rev is the Bayesian counterpart of the glottochronology bias of Section 9.2.5. The data were simulated with strong gamma-distributed rate variation among characters (\(\alpha = 0.5\)). They are dated with only the young calibration C1, so the root age is extrapolated, as in a glottochronological date. The script is run with discrete-gamma rate variation (four categories, \(\alpha\) estimated) and without it. Ignoring the variation underestimates the amount of change on long paths and should make the deep dates too young (Equation (C.8)).

################################################################################
# 15_gamma_rate_variation_dating_bias.Rev
#
# Model    : strict clock dating with and without gamma-distributed rate
#            variation among meanings (cognate characters). Data simulated
#            with strong among-character rate variation (alpha = 0.5). Fitting
#            a model without it underestimates the amount of change on long
#            paths (saturation is mistaken for less change), which biases
#            deep node ages young: the Bayesian analogue of the glottochronology
#            bias of Equation clocks-gamma. Only the young calibration C1 is
#            used, so the root age is extrapolated as in a glottochronological
#            date. Fixed true topology.
#              gamma   : Gamma(alpha, alpha) site rates, 4 discrete categories
#              nogamma : all characters share one rate
# Book     : Ch. 9 "Rate variation among meanings biases dates"
#            (clocks-glotto-gamma); "Rate variation across meanings" (clocks-meanings)
# Estimates: root age, clock rate, alpha
# Data     : data/time/clock_gamma.nex (12 languages, 600 characters, alpha = 0.5)
# Runtime  : ~1 min per model
# Usage    : cd revbayes && rb analyses/time/15_gamma_rate_variation_dating_bias.Rev --args MODEL [n_gen]
#            MODEL in {gamma, nogamma}
################################################################################

seed(1515)
model_name = "gamma"
n_gen = 15000
if (args.size() > 1) model_name = args[2]
if (args.size() > 2) n_gen = int(args[3])
out_dir = "output/time/15_gamma_rate_variation_dating_bias/" + model_name + "_"

data <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/time/clock_gamma.nex")
taxa <- data.taxa()
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

root_age ~ dnUniform(0.5, 30.0)
birth_rate ~ dnExponential(1.0)
timetree ~ dnBDP(lambda=birth_rate, mu=0.0, rho=1.0, rootAge=root_age, taxa=taxa)
start_tree <- readTrees("data/time/tree12_start.tre")[1]
root_age.setValue(start_tree.rootAge())
timetree.setValue(start_tree)
moves.append( mvScale(birth_rate, lambda=1.0, tune=true, weight=1.0) )
moves.append( mvSlide(root_age, delta=0.5, tune=true, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvTreeScale(tree=timetree, rootAge=root_age, delta=0.5, tune=true, weight=3.0) )
moves.append( mvNodeTimeSlideUniform(timetree, weight=15.0) )
moves.append( mvSubtreeScale(timetree, weight=5.0) )

# young calibration only
source("data/time/calibrations_tree12.Rev")
age_C1 := tmrca(timetree, clade_C1)
obs_C1 ~ dnSoftBoundUniformNormal(min=C1_min - age_C1, max=C1_max - age_C1, sd=C1_sd, p=0.95)
obs_C1.clamp(0.0)

clock_rate ~ dnExponential(2.0)
moves.append( mvScale(clock_rate, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=5.0) )
up_down = mvUpDownScale(lambda=0.3, tune=true, weight=5.0)
up_down.addVariable(root_age, up=true)
up_down.addVariable(timetree, up=true)
up_down.addVariable(clock_rate, up=false)
moves.append( up_down )

pi ~ dnDirichlet(v(1, 1))
pi1 := pi[2]
Q := fnF81(pi)
moves.append( mvBetaSimplex(pi, alpha=20, tune=true, weight=2.0) )

if (model_name == "gamma") {
  alpha ~ dnExponential(1.0)
  site_rates := fnDiscretizeGamma(alpha, alpha, 4)
  moves.append( mvScale(alpha, lambda=0.5, tune=true, weight=3.0) )
  seq ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree=timetree, Q=Q, branchRates=clock_rate, siteRates=site_rates, type="Standard")
} else {
  seq ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree=timetree, Q=Q, branchRates=clock_rate, type="Standard")
}
seq.clamp(data)

mymodel = model(timetree)
monitors.append( mnModel(filename=out_dir + "model.log", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=5000, root_age, clock_rate) )
mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=n_gen, tuningInterval=200)

q()
Model Parameter Truth Post. mean HPD low HPD high ESS Status
strict clock + Gamma(4) among-meaning rates root_age 6.00 4.606 1.490 8.310 799 pass
strict clock + Gamma(4) among-meaning rates clock_rate 0.15 0.201 0.082 0.391 873 pass
strict clock + Gamma(4) among-meaning rates alpha 0.50 0.449 0.330 0.577 815 pass
strict clock, no among-meaning rate variation (misspecified) root_age 6.00 2.309 0.726 3.947 676 info-fail

With gamma rate variation the root is recovered (posterior mean 4.6, HPD 1.5 to 8.3 ky; truth 6) and so is \(\alpha\) (0.45; truth 0.5). Without it the root is far too young (2.3 ky, HPD 0.7 to 3.9 ky), which is the bias predicted by Equation (C.8).

H.4.16 Models not implemented

Three models from Chapters 9, 10 and 16 have no script here.

  • Penalized likelihood and rate smoothing (Section 9.5.5) are not Bayesian. They are covered by ape::chronos() in the book itself.
  • The optimized relaxed clock (Section 9.5.4) is a set of MCMC proposals for the UCLN model rather than a different model. Script 02 uses the corresponding RevBayes moves (mvRateAgeBetaShift, mvUpDownScale).
  • Stratigraphic-range FBD models (dnFBDRP), skyline FBD models with a sampling rate that changes when writing appears (the timeline and psiTimeline arguments of dnFBDP), HiSSE and calibration cross-validation can all be expressed with the RevBayes 1.4.1 functions listed above. They are left as extensions, because verifying them would need either more ancient languages or much larger trees than these small test data sets have.

H.5 Phylogeography, ancestral states and comparative models

This section documents the RevBayes (Höhna et al. 2016) scripts for the trait models of Chapters 11, 12, 13 and 14: discrete and continuous phylogeography, range evolution, Mk models and ancestral states, stochastic character mapping, hidden rates, correlated evolution, Brownian motion and its relatives, phylogenetic regression and signal, threshold and spatial models. Each model has one standalone script in revbayes/analyses/traits/, run on a small data set simulated with known parameter values by revbayes/data/sim_traits.R (true values in revbayes/data/traits/true_values.csv); revbayes/tests/check_traits.R reads the output, computes posterior means, 95% highest-posterior-density (HPD) intervals and effective sample sizes (ESS, coda), checks whether the truth is covered and runs the model-specific checks described below, writing revbayes/tests/results_traits.csv.

Conventions. Most scripts condition on one fixed, known time tree of 16 languages (data/traits/tree16.tre, a Yule tree with root age 4; time is in millennia, so rates are per thousand years). Three scripts integrate over tree uncertainty instead (13, 14 and 22). Coordinates are planar, in units of 100 km. Scripts are run from revbayes/:

cd revbayes
Rscript data/sim_traits.R                                # simulate all data sets
rb analyses/traits/05_mk_asr.Rev                         # one analysis, default settings
rb analyses/traits/02_continuous_phylogeo_bm.Rev --args 20000   # longer chain
bash tests/run_traits.sh                                 # all analyses, 2 at a time
Rscript tests/check_traits.R                             # writes tests/results_traits.csv

The first command-line argument after --args is the number of MCMC generations. Several scripts fit more than one model; each then also estimates the marginal likelihood of every model by stepping-stone and path sampling (powerPosterior, Chapter 6) and writes them to marginal_likelihoods.csv in its output folder.

Two RevBayes pitfalls shaped these scripts. First, model(x) collects every node connected to x, including through shared constant nodes (a tree object, a prior constant such as rate <- 2.0) and through the elements of one Rev vector (x[1] and x[2]). Two models built in the same script that share such a node are silently merged, and a power posterior then adds their likelihoods. Each model in a multi-model script therefore has its own tree copy and its own variable names. Second, inside a loop an index such as i <- n - j is a constant node that is re-evaluated when it is reassigned, so every distribution created with tree.branchLength(i) ends up using the last value; loops therefore run over the loop variable itself (for (i in (n - 1):1)).

The verification standard is the one used throughout this appendix: the script runs; the 95% HPD interval of each key parameter contains the simulated value (or the failure is explained); ESS is reported (100 or more counts as adequate); model comparisons are reported whether or not they pick the generating model; and, where possible, the Bayesian result is compared with an independent calculation (maximum likelihood from ape, phytools, geiger or nlme, or an exact numerical result). With 16 languages and one character, many parameters are only weakly identified: wide intervals that contain the truth are the expected outcome, and so are model comparisons that cannot separate similar models. The table summarizes the checks; “miss” marks a check that did not come out as the generating model would predict, “expected_miss” a failure that the book itself predicts (script 16), and “warn_ess” an ESS below 100. The text explains each one.

H.5.1 Discrete phylogeography with BSSVS

01_discrete_phylogeo_bssvs.Rev implements the discrete phylogeography of Section 11.4.1 with Bayesian stochastic search variable selection (Section 11.4.2, Equation (11.3)). Four regions A-D lie on a line, and the data were simulated with only the three adjacent routes (AB, BC, CD) active, at rate 0.3 per millennium, from a homeland in A. Each of the six symmetric route rates is a reversible-jump mixture of a point mass at zero (route absent) and an exponential rate, so the indicators \(\delta_{ij}\) are the moves of a reversible-jump sampler (dnReversibleJumpMixture + mvRJSwitch). The book’s prior puts Poisson(\(\ln 2\)) plus \(K - 1\) on the number of active routes; RevBayes has no built-in prior on the sum of indicators, so the script uses independent indicators with the same expected number of active routes, i.e. prior inclusion probability \(q = (\ln 2 + K - 1)/(K(K-1)/2) = 0.62\), which makes the book’s Bayes factor formula exact. The root region is sampled with mnJointConditionalAncestralState (two runs).

################################################################################
# 01_discrete_phylogeo_bssvs.Rev
#
# Model:    Discrete phylogeography. The region of a lineage (K = 4 regions,
#           A-D) evolves as a symmetric CTMC whose route rates are switched on
#           and off by Bayesian stochastic search variable selection (BSSVS),
#           implemented with reversible-jump mixtures: each route rate q_ij is
#           0 (route absent, delta_ij = 0) or drawn from an exponential prior
#           (delta_ij = 1).
# Book:     Chapter 11, "Locations as states of a Markov chain"
#           (#phylogeography-ctmc) and "Bayesian stochastic search variable
#           selection" (#phylogeography-bssvs), Eqs. phylogeography-bssvs and
#           phylogeography-bf.
# Estimates: posterior inclusion probability of each route (-> Bayes factor),
#           route rates, and the posterior of the root (homeland) region.
# Data:     data/traits/regions.nex on the fixed time tree data/traits/tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/01_discrete_phylogeo_bssvs.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 40 s (2 runs x 10,000 generations)
################################################################################

seed(1101)
n_gen = 10000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/traits/01_discrete_phylogeo_bssvs/"
t_start = time("seconds")

tree    <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
regions <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/traits/regions.nex")

K        <- 4
n_routes <- K * (K - 1) / 2
# Prior inclusion probability of one route, q = (ln 2 + K - 1) / (K(K-1)/2).
# The book's BSSVS prior puts Poisson(ln 2) + (K - 1) on the number of active
# routes; we use independent indicators with the same expected number of
# active routes, so that the Bayes factor formula of the book applies exactly.
q_incl <- (ln(2) + K - 1) / n_routes

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

# route rates in the order AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD
for (k in 1:n_routes) {
    r[k] ~ dnReversibleJumpMixture(0.0, dnExponential(1.0), p = 1.0 - q_incl)
    r[k].setValue(0.5)
    delta[k] := ifelse(r[k] > 0.0, 1, 0)
    moves.append( mvRJSwitch(r[k], weight = 1.0) )
    moves.append( mvScale(r[k], lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
}
n_active := sum(delta)

# symmetric 4 x 4 matrix; off-diagonal elements in row order
Q := fnFreeK([ r[1], r[2], r[3],
               r[1], r[4], r[5],
               r[2], r[4], r[6],
               r[3], r[5], r[6] ], rescaled = FALSE)

root_freq <- simplex(rep(1, K))         # flat prior on the homeland region
ctmc ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree, Q = Q, rootFrequencies = root_freq,
                   type = "Standard", nSites = 1)
ctmc.clamp(regions)

mymodel = model(Q)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "model.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree, ctmc = ctmc,
                 type = "Standard", withTips = FALSE, withStartStates = FALSE,
                 filename = out_dir + "states.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, n_active) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, monitors, moves, nruns = 2, combine = "none")
mymcmc.burnin(generations = 2000, tuningInterval = 100)
mymcmc.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)

write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()

BSSVS discrete phylogeography delta_AC 0.0 0.525 NA NA 1902 pass
BSSVS discrete phylogeography delta_AD 0.0 0.586 NA NA 1881 pass
BSSVS discrete phylogeography delta_BC 1.0 0.580 NA NA 3581 miss
BSSVS discrete phylogeography delta_BD 0.0 0.642 NA NA 1828 miss
BSSVS discrete phylogeography delta_CD 1.0 0.787 NA NA 1902 pass
BSSVS discrete phylogeography r[1] 0.3 1.335 0 3.301 1902 pass
BSSVS discrete phylogeography r[2] 0.0 0.371 0 1.756 1753 pass
BSSVS discrete phylogeography r[3] 0.0 0.442 0 1.916 1902 pass

For indicators, the posterior mean is the posterior inclusion probability and a check passes when the Bayes factor points the right way (BF > 1 for a true route, < 1 for an absent one). Route AB is decisively supported (BF about 20) and CD positively (BF about 2), while BC and the absent route BD are both near the prior (BF 0.9 and 1.1): one location character on 16 tips carries little information about six routes, exactly the weak identifiability that Section 11.4.2 warns about. The root posterior puts the most mass on the true homeland A (0.33, with B close behind), in line with the maximum-likelihood (ML) marginal from ape::ace.

H.5.2 Continuous phylogeography: bivariate Brownian diffusion

02_continuous_phylogeo_bm.Rev implements Equation (11.5) (Section 11.5.1): the coordinates of every node are parameters, each child is bivariate normal around its parent with covariance \(t_c \boldsymbol\Sigma\), and the tip locations are clamped. The diffusion matrix is built from two rates and a correlation with fnVarCovar, and the root location (the homeland) has a vague bivariate normal prior. Since the internal locations are sampled, the same script gives ancestral locations for every proto-language.

################################################################################
# 02_continuous_phylogeo_bm.Rev
#
# Model:    Continuous phylogeography by bivariate Brownian diffusion of
#           projected coordinates (x = km east, y = km north, units of 100 km).
#           Every node location is a parameter (data augmentation):
#               x_c | x_a ~ N_2(x_a, t_c * Sigma),
#           Sigma = [[s_x^2, rho s_x s_y], [rho s_x s_y, s_y^2]].
#           Tip locations are clamped to the observed coordinates.
# Book:     Chapter 11, "Brownian diffusion" (#phylogeography-bm),
#           Eq. phylogeography-bm and phylogeography-mvn.
# Estimates: root location (homeland), diffusion rates s_x, s_y and rho;
#           ancestral locations of all internal nodes.
# Data:     data/traits/coords_bm.tsv on data/traits/tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/02_continuous_phylogeo_bm.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 2 minutes (2 runs x 7,000 generations)
################################################################################

seed(1102)
n_gen = 7000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/traits/02_continuous_phylogeo_bm/"
t_start = time("seconds")

tree   <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
coords = readDataDelimitedFile("data/traits/coords_bm.tsv", header = TRUE, delimiter = "\t")
n_tips  <- tree.ntips()
n_nodes <- tree.nnodes()
root_idx <- tree.getRootIndex()

# observed tip coordinates, indexed by RevBayes node index
for (r in 1:coords.size()) {
    obs[tree.tipIndex(coords[r][1])] <- [ coords[r][2], coords[r][3] ]
}

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

# diffusion matrix
sigma_x ~ dnLognormal(0.0, 1.0)
sigma_y ~ dnLognormal(0.0, 1.0)
rho     ~ dnUniform(-1.0, 1.0)
Sigma := fnVarCovar([sigma_x, sigma_y], [rho])
moves.append( mvScale(sigma_x, lambda = 0.3, weight = 3.0) )
moves.append( mvScale(sigma_y, lambda = 0.3, weight = 3.0) )
moves.append( mvSlide(rho, delta = 0.2, weight = 3.0) )

# root location: vague bivariate normal prior (sd = 10, i.e. 1000 km)
# (mvVectorSlide element indices are 0-based)
loc[root_idx] ~ dnMultivariateNormal([0.0, 0.0], covariance = fnVarCovar([10.0, 10.0], [0.0]))
loc[root_idx].setValue([0.0, 0.0])
moves.append( mvVectorSlide(loc[root_idx], delta = 0.5, weight = 3.0) )
moves.append( mvVectorSlide(loc[root_idx], elements = [0], delta = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
moves.append( mvVectorSlide(loc[root_idx], elements = [1], delta = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )

# all other nodes, from the root down (parents have larger indices than children)
# NB: the loop index must be the loop variable itself (a constant node such as
# `i <- n_nodes - j` would be re-evaluated when it is reassigned).
for (i in (n_nodes - 1):1) {
    loc[i] ~ dnMultivariateNormal(loc[tree.parent(i)], covariance = Sigma,
                                  scale = tree.branchLength(i))
    if (i <= n_tips) {
        loc[i].clamp(obs[i])
    } else {
        loc[i].setValue([0.0, 0.0])
        moves.append( mvVectorSlide(loc[i], elements = [0], delta = 0.3, weight = 1.0) )
        moves.append( mvVectorSlide(loc[i], elements = [1], delta = 0.3, weight = 1.0) )
    }
}

root_x := loc[root_idx][1]
root_y := loc[root_idx][2]

mymodel = model(Sigma)

monitors.append( mnFile(sigma_x, sigma_y, rho, root_x, root_y,
                        filename = out_dir + "model.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, root_x, root_y, sigma_x) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, monitors, moves, nruns = 2, combine = "none")
mymcmc.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mymcmc.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)

write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()
Model Parameter Truth Post. mean HPD low HPD high ESS Status
bivariate BM diffusion root_x 2.0 2.223 -0.176 4.337 694 pass
bivariate BM diffusion root_y -1.0 -2.342 -3.982 -0.576 588 pass
bivariate BM diffusion sigma_x 1.0 1.166 0.761 1.624 739 pass
bivariate BM diffusion sigma_y 0.7 0.815 0.555 1.124 863 pass
bivariate BM diffusion rho 0.4 0.480 0.130 0.829 1200 pass
bivariate BM diffusion root_vs_GLS NA 0.108 NA NA NA pass

All five parameters are covered. The posterior mean homeland agrees with the generalized least-squares root of Equation (11.6), computed independently in R, to within about 10 km (root_vs_GLS). That estimate lies about 140 km south of the simulated homeland, which sits near the edge of the 95% interval: the GLS root is a weighted average of this particular realization of the walk, and the interval is honest about it.

H.5.3 Relaxed random walk

03_relaxed_random_walk.Rev implements the lognormal relaxed random walk of Section 11.5.2 (Equation (11.7)). Each branch has a variance multiplier \(\phi_b\) with mean one, and the internal locations are integrated out by dnPhyloMultivariateBrownianREML (the per-branch argument of that distribution is a standard-deviation multiplier, so it receives \(\sqrt{\phi_b}\)). The multipliers use a non-centered parameterization, \(\phi_b = \exp(-s^2/2 + s z_b)\) with \(z_b \sim N(0, 1)\). The model is unchanged, but a first, centered version got stuck in the “funnel” near \(s = 0\) (ESS below 20). The script also reports a weighted diffusion rate.

################################################################################
# 03_relaxed_random_walk.Rev
#
# Model:    Relaxed random walk (RRW) for continuous coordinates. Bivariate
#           Brownian diffusion with diffusion matrix Sigma, where every branch b
#           has its own variance multiplier phi_b ~ Lognormal(-s^2/2, s) (mean 1):
#               x_c | x_a, phi_b ~ N_2(x_a, phi_b * t_c * Sigma).
#           The root and internal locations are integrated out analytically
#           (restricted likelihood, dnPhyloMultivariateBrownianREML).
# Book:     Chapter 11, "The relaxed random walk" (#phylogeography-rrw),
#           Eq. phylogeography-rrw (lognormal version).
# Estimates: sigma_x, sigma_y, rho, the spread s of the log multipliers,
#           branch multipliers phi_b, and the weighted diffusion rate.
# Data:     data/traits/coords_rrw.nex on data/traits/tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/03_relaxed_random_walk.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 1 minute
################################################################################

seed(1103)
n_gen = 30000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/traits/03_relaxed_random_walk/"
t_start = time("seconds")

tree   <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
coords <- readContinuousCharacterData("data/traits/coords_rrw.nex")
n_branches <- tree.nnodes() - 1

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

sigma_x ~ dnLognormal(0.0, 1.0)
sigma_y ~ dnLognormal(0.0, 1.0)
rho     ~ dnUniform(-1.0, 1.0)
Sigma := fnVarCovar([sigma_x, sigma_y], [rho])
moves.append( mvScale(sigma_x, lambda = 0.3, weight = 2.0) )
moves.append( mvScale(sigma_y, lambda = 0.3, weight = 2.0) )
moves.append( mvSlide(rho, delta = 0.2, weight = 2.0) )

# lognormal branch multipliers with mean one; s has an exponential prior.
# Non-centred parameterization, phi_b = exp(-s^2/2 + s z_b) with z_b ~ N(0, 1),
# which is the same model as phi_b ~ Lognormal(-s^2/2, s) but avoids the
# "funnel" between s and the phi_b that traps a centred sampler near s = 0.
s_phi ~ dnExponential(1.0)
moves.append( mvScale(s_phi, lambda = 0.3, weight = 3.0) )
m_phi := -0.5 * s_phi * s_phi
for (b in 1:n_branches) {
    z_phi[b] ~ dnNormal(0.0, 1.0)
    moves.append( mvSlide(z_phi[b], delta = 1.0, weight = 1.0) )
    phi[b] := exp(m_phi + s_phi * z_phi[b])
    # the REML likelihood takes per-branch standard-deviation multipliers
    br_sd[b] := sqrt(phi[b])
}

X ~ dnPhyloMultivariateBrownianREML(tree, branchRates = br_sd, rateMatrix = Sigma)
X.clamp(coords)

# weighted diffusion rate: expected squared displacement per unit time in the
# plane is (sigma_x^2 + sigma_y^2) times the time-weighted mean multiplier
for (b in 1:n_branches) bl[b] <- tree.branchLength(b)
total_time <- sum(bl)
for (b in 1:n_branches) w_phi[b] := phi[b] * bl[b] / total_time
mean_phi := sum(w_phi)
weighted_diffusion := (sigma_x * sigma_x + sigma_y * sigma_y) * mean_phi / 4.0

mymodel = model(Sigma)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "model.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, sigma_x, sigma_y, s_phi) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, monitors, moves, nruns = 1)
mymcmc.burnin(generations = 2000, tuningInterval = 100)
mymcmc.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)

write(tree, filename = out_dir + "tree_index.txt")
write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()
Model Parameter Truth Post. mean HPD low HPD high ESS Status
relaxed random walk (lognormal) sigma_x 0.8 0.756 0.444 1.145 2129 pass
relaxed random walk (lognormal) sigma_y 0.8 0.665 0.387 0.999 2119 pass
relaxed random walk (lognormal) rho 0.3 0.390 -0.112 0.800 2851 pass
relaxed random walk (lognormal) s_phi 0.8 0.503 0.001 1.315 1078 pass

The diffusion parameters and the spread \(s\) are covered. The individual branch multipliers are barely identified with 16 tips: the rank correlation between the realized and posterior-mean multipliers is weak but positive.

H.5.4 DEC range evolution

04_dec.Rev implements the dispersal-extinction-cladogenesis model described in the biologist’s toolbox of Chapter 11 (Section 11.12; Ree et al. (2005); Ree and Smith (2008)), for three areas. The anagenetic rate matrix comes from fnDECRateMatrix (dispersal rate \(d\) per area pair, local extinction rate \(e\); the null range is excluded, so a single-area range cannot be lost) and cladogenesis from fnDECCladoProbs with subset sympatry and allopatry (probType = "class": a class is chosen with probability clado_probs, then a pattern uniformly within it, which is exactly how sim_traits.R simulates). Ranges are coded as presence/absence per area and converted with formatDiscreteCharacterData(..., "DEC").

################################################################################
# 04_dec.Rev
#
# Model:    DEC (dispersal-extinction-cladogenesis) range evolution, three areas
#           A, B, C. Anagenetic CTMC on ranges (dispersal rate d per area pair,
#           local extinction rate e per area; the null range is excluded, so a
#           single-area range cannot be lost), plus cladogenetic range
#           inheritance at nodes: narrow sympatry for one-area ranges, and
#           subset sympatry ("s") or allopatry ("a") for wider ranges.
# Book:     Chapter 11, "From the biologist's toolbox" (#phylogeography-toolbox),
#           the DEC paragraph (Ree & Smith 2008), Bayesian version of Landis et al. 2013.
# Estimates: d, e, the cladogenetic class probability of subset sympatry, and
#           the ancestral range at the root.
# Data:     data/traits/ranges.nex (presence/absence in A, B, C) on tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/04_dec.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 1 minute
################################################################################

seed(1104)
n_gen = 10000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/traits/04_dec/"
t_start = time("seconds")

tree   <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
rng01  <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/traits/ranges.nex")
n_areas  <- rng01.nchar()
n_states <- 2^n_areas
rng = formatDiscreteCharacterData(rng01, "DEC", n_states)

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

dispersal   ~ dnExponential(2.0)
extirpation ~ dnExponential(2.0)
moves.append( mvScale(dispersal,   lambda = 0.5, weight = 3.0) )
moves.append( mvScale(extirpation, lambda = 0.5, weight = 3.0) )

for (i in 1:n_areas) {
    for (j in 1:n_areas) {
        dr[i][j] := dispersal
        er[i][j] <- 0.0
    }
}
for (i in 1:n_areas) er[i][i] := extirpation

Q_DEC := fnDECRateMatrix(dispersalRates = dr, extirpationRates = er, nullRange = "Exclude")

# cladogenesis: probability of subset sympatry vs allopatry (class weights)
clado_probs ~ dnDirichlet([1, 1])
moves.append( mvSimplexElementScale(clado_probs, alpha = 10.0, weight = 2.0) )
p_sympatry := clado_probs[1]
P_DEC := fnDECCladoProbs(eventProbs = clado_probs, eventTypes = ["s", "a"],
                         numCharacters = n_areas, probType = "class")

# flat prior over the non-empty ranges at the root
rf <- rep(1, n_states)
rf[1] <- 0
root_freq <- simplex(rf)

m_bg ~ dnPhyloCTMCClado(tree = tree, Q = Q_DEC, cladoProbs = P_DEC,
                        rootFrequencies = root_freq, type = "NaturalNumbers", nSites = 1)
m_bg.clamp(rng)

mymodel = model(m_bg)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "model.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree, ctmc = m_bg, type = "NaturalNumbers",
                 withTips = TRUE, withStartStates = TRUE,
                 filename = out_dir + "states.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, dispersal, extirpation) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, monitors, moves, nruns = 1)
mymcmc.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mymcmc.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)

write(tree, filename = out_dir + "tree_index.txt")
write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()
Model Parameter Truth Post. mean HPD low HPD high ESS Status
DEC dispersal 0.40 0.577 0.193 1.132 951 pass
DEC extirpation 0.15 0.300 0.001 0.853 951 pass
DEC p_sympatry 0.50 0.395 0.004 0.754 951 pass
DEC root_state 0.00 0.176 NA NA NA pass

\(d\), \(e\) and the cladogenetic probability are covered. The check script also verifies the state coding (the sampled tip states equal the observed ranges). The root range is nearly uniform over the seven possible ranges. The true range {A} is in the 95% credible set but is not the most probable range: 16 tips and three areas say little about the root.

H.5.5 Mk models and ancestral states for word order

05_mk_asr.Rev fits the Mk models of Section 12.4.1 to a three-state word-order feature (SOV, SVO, VSO) simulated under an ordered model (SOV \(\leftrightarrow\) SVO \(\leftrightarrow\) VSO) from an SOV root: equal rates (ER), all rates different (ARD) and the ordered model, each with marginal ancestral states (Section 12.4.2) and stepping-stone marginal likelihoods.

################################################################################
# 05_mk_asr.Rev
#
# Model:    Mk models for a three-state feature, basic word order
#           (0 = SOV, 1 = SVO, 2 = VSO): equal rates (ER, one rate),
#           all rates different (ARD, six rates) and an ordered model
#           (SOV <-> SVO <-> VSO, four rates, no direct SOV <-> VSO change).
#           For each model: MCMC with marginal ancestral states at the root and
#           at every internal node, and the marginal likelihood by
#           stepping-stone and path sampling (power posteriors).
# Book:     Chapter 12, "The Mk model" (#asr-mk), "Marginal reconstruction"
#           (#asr-marginal), "Bayesian ASR" (#asr-bayes), Section #asr-wordorder;
#           Chapter 6 for marginal likelihoods.
# Estimates: rates, root state posterior, log marginal likelihoods of the three
#           models (the data were generated under the ordered model).
# Data:     data/traits/wordorder.nex on tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/05_mk_asr.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 1.5 minutes
################################################################################

seed(1105)
n_gen = 10000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
n_cats  = 24          # power-posterior stones
pp_gen  = 1000        # generations per stone
out_dir = "output/traits/05_mk_asr/"
t_start = time("seconds")

# NB: every model gets its OWN copy of the tree (and of the root frequencies
# and prior constants):
# model() collects every node connected to its argument, including through
# shared constant nodes, so models that share a tree object would be merged
# into one graph and their likelihoods added in the power posteriors.
tree     <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
tree_er  <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
tree_ard <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
tree_ord <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
wo   <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/traits/wordorder.nex")
# exponential prior on each rate, rate 2 (mean 0.5 per kyr); written inline in
# each model because a shared constant node would also join the model graphs

write("model,lnML_stepping_stone,lnML_path_sampling\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv")

############################ ER
q_er ~ dnExponential(2.0)
mv_er = VectorMoves()
mv_er.append( mvScale(q_er, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
Q_er := fnFreeK([q_er, q_er, q_er, q_er, q_er, q_er], rescaled = FALSE)
ctmc_er ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree_er, Q = Q_er, rootFrequencies = simplex([1, 1, 1]), type = "Standard", nSites = 1)
ctmc_er.clamp(wo)
mod_er = model(Q_er)
mn_er = VectorMonitors()
mn_er.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "ER_model.log", printgen = 10) )
mn_er.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree_er, ctmc = ctmc_er, type = "Standard",
              withTips = FALSE, withStartStates = FALSE, filename = out_dir + "ER_states.log", printgen = 10) )
mcmc_er = mcmc(mod_er, mn_er, mv_er, nruns = 1)
mcmc_er.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mcmc_er.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)
pp_er = powerPosterior(mod_er, mv_er, VectorMonitors(), out_dir + "ER_powp.log", cats = n_cats, sampleFreq = 10)
pp_er.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
pp_er.run(generations = pp_gen)
ss_er = steppingStoneSampler(out_dir + "ER_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
ps_er = pathSampler(out_dir + "ER_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
write("ER", ss_er, ps_er, filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE, separator = ",")
write("\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE)

############################ ARD
for (k in 1:6) {
    q_ard[k] ~ dnExponential(2.0)
}
mv_ard = VectorMoves()
for (k in 1:6) mv_ard.append( mvScale(q_ard[k], lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
Q_ard := fnFreeK(q_ard, rescaled = FALSE)
ctmc_ard ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree_ard, Q = Q_ard, rootFrequencies = simplex([1, 1, 1]), type = "Standard", nSites = 1)
ctmc_ard.clamp(wo)
mod_ard = model(Q_ard)
mn_ard = VectorMonitors()
mn_ard.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "ARD_model.log", printgen = 10) )
mn_ard.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree_ard, ctmc = ctmc_ard, type = "Standard",
               withTips = FALSE, withStartStates = FALSE, filename = out_dir + "ARD_states.log", printgen = 10) )
mcmc_ard = mcmc(mod_ard, mn_ard, mv_ard, nruns = 1)
mcmc_ard.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mcmc_ard.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)
pp_ard = powerPosterior(mod_ard, mv_ard, VectorMonitors(), out_dir + "ARD_powp.log", cats = n_cats, sampleFreq = 10)
pp_ard.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
pp_ard.run(generations = pp_gen)
ss_ard = steppingStoneSampler(out_dir + "ARD_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
ps_ard = pathSampler(out_dir + "ARD_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
write("ARD", ss_ard, ps_ard, filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE, separator = ",")
write("\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE)

############################ ordered (SOV <-> SVO <-> VSO)
q_sov_svo ~ dnExponential(2.0)
q_svo_sov ~ dnExponential(2.0)
q_svo_vso ~ dnExponential(2.0)
q_vso_svo ~ dnExponential(2.0)
mv_ord = VectorMoves()
mv_ord.append( mvScale(q_sov_svo, lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
mv_ord.append( mvScale(q_svo_sov, lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
mv_ord.append( mvScale(q_svo_vso, lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
mv_ord.append( mvScale(q_vso_svo, lambda = 0.5, weight = 1.0) )
Q_ord := fnFreeK([q_sov_svo, 0.0, q_svo_sov, q_svo_vso, 0.0, q_vso_svo], rescaled = FALSE)
ctmc_ord ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree_ord, Q = Q_ord, rootFrequencies = simplex([1, 1, 1]), type = "Standard", nSites = 1)
ctmc_ord.clamp(wo)
mod_ord = model(Q_ord)
mn_ord = VectorMonitors()
mn_ord.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "ORD_model.log", printgen = 10) )
mn_ord.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree_ord, ctmc = ctmc_ord, type = "Standard",
               withTips = FALSE, withStartStates = FALSE, filename = out_dir + "ORD_states.log", printgen = 10) )
mcmc_ord = mcmc(mod_ord, mn_ord, mv_ord, nruns = 1)
mcmc_ord.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mcmc_ord.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)
pp_ord = powerPosterior(mod_ord, mv_ord, VectorMonitors(), out_dir + "ORD_powp.log", cats = n_cats, sampleFreq = 10)
pp_ord.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
pp_ord.run(generations = pp_gen)
ss_ord = steppingStoneSampler(out_dir + "ORD_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
ps_ord = pathSampler(out_dir + "ORD_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
write("ORD", ss_ord, ps_ord, filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE, separator = ",")
write("\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE)

write(tree, filename = out_dir + "tree_index.txt")
write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()

Two exact checks are possible for the one-parameter ER model. Integrating the likelihood numerically over the rate gives a log marginal likelihood of \(-12.526\); stepping-stone sampling gives \(-12.531\). The exact Bayesian root probabilities (0.11/0.78/0.11) match the MCMC values (0.12/0.76/0.12). The empirical-Bayes root from ape::ace (0.02/0.96/0.02) is much more confident, as Section 12.4.2 predicts, because it fixes the rate at its ML value. The tips are mostly SVO, so every model puts most mass on an SVO root even though the simulated history started in SOV; SOV stays in the 95% credible set. The three models’ marginal likelihoods lie within 1.1 log units of each other (ARD \(-11.42\), ordered \(-11.64\), ER \(-12.53\)). One character on 16 tips cannot separate them, so the “best model” check is a miss, as expected.

H.5.6 Stochastic character mapping

06_stochastic_mapping.Rev fits a two-state Mk model and draws one complete character history per sample with mnStochasticCharacterMap (Section 12.6), so the rates are integrated over rather than fixed. check_traits.R parses the SIMMAP strings (which list the tip end of each branch first) to count changes of each type (Markov jumps) and to sum the time spent in each state (rewards; Section 11.4.3). It compares them with the history that actually generated the data and with phytools::make.simmap.

################################################################################
# 06_stochastic_mapping.Rev
#
# Model:    Two-state Mk model (all rates different, q01 and q10) for a binary
#           feature, with stochastic character mapping: at every sampled
#           iteration a complete history of the character along all branches
#           is drawn from its posterior given the tip states, the tree and the
#           current rates (the rates themselves are integrated over by MCMC).
# Book:     Chapter 12, "Stochastic character mapping" (#asr-simmap),
#           Eq. asr-simmap-node; Chapter 11, "Markov jumps and rewards"
#           (#phylogeography-jumps).
# Estimates: q01, q10; posterior distribution of the number of changes of each
#           type (Markov jumps) and of the time spent in each state (rewards,
#           dwell times); compared with the realized true history.
# Data:     data/traits/binary_map.nex on tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/06_stochastic_mapping.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 10 s
################################################################################

seed(1106)
n_gen = 10000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
out_dir = "output/traits/06_stochastic_mapping/"
t_start = time("seconds")

tree <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
feat <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/traits/binary_map.nex")

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()

q01 ~ dnExponential(2.0)
q10 ~ dnExponential(2.0)
moves.append( mvScale(q01, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
moves.append( mvScale(q10, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
Q := fnFreeK([q01, q10], rescaled = FALSE)

ctmc ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree, Q = Q, rootFrequencies = simplex([1, 1]),
                   type = "Standard", nSites = 1)
ctmc.clamp(feat)

mymodel = model(Q)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "model.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnStochasticCharacterMap(ctmc = ctmc, filename = out_dir + "maps.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(tree = tree, ctmc = ctmc, type = "Standard",
                 withTips = TRUE, withStartStates = FALSE, filename = out_dir + "states.log", printgen = 10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, q01, q10) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, monitors, moves, nruns = 1)
mymcmc.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mymcmc.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)

# summary map on the fixed tree (posterior probabilities of states along branches)
anc_trace = readAncestralStateTrace(out_dir + "maps.log")
characterMapTree(tree, anc_trace, character_file = out_dir + "map_summary_character.tree",
                 posterior_file = out_dir + "map_summary_posterior.tree", burnin = 0.1, reconstruction = "marginal")

write(tree, filename = out_dir + "tree_index.txt")
write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()

Mk ARD + stochastic map q10 0.250 0.221 0.018 0.560 951 pass
stochastic character mapping n01 4.000 4.242 0.000 12.000 1045 pass
stochastic character mapping n10 3.000 3.835 0.000 9.000 951 pass
stochastic character mapping n 7.000 8.077 2.000 21.000 951 pass
stochastic character mapping dwell_0 6.376 5.175 0.962 11.924 951 pass
stochastic character mapping dwell_1 19.825 21.025 14.277 25.239 951 pass

The realized numbers of changes (4 gains, 3 losses) and dwell times lie well inside their posterior intervals, and the posterior means agree with the empirical-Bayes maps from phytools (8.1 vs 8.0 changes on average). The posterior expected number of changes exceeds the parsimony minimum, as the note in Section 12.6 anticipates.

H.5.7 Hidden-rates model

07_hidden_rates.Rev implements the hidden-rates model of Section 12.7 (Equation (D.9)) with a slow and a fast category. The data are expanded with expandCharacters(2) so that each observed state is ambiguous between its two hidden copies. The \(4 \times 4\) matrix is built with fnFreeK, because in RevBayes 1.4.1 fnHiddenStateRateMatrix applies the same observed-state rates in every category. To avoid label switching, the fast rate is the slow rate plus a positive increment. One binary feature on 16 tips carries almost no information about hidden rates, so 40 independent features were simulated under the same process. The model is compared with a one-category Mk model by stepping-stone sampling.

################################################################################
# 07_hidden_rates.Rev
#
# Model:    Hidden-rates model (HRM; covarion-like) for binary features.
#           Each observed state (0/1) is paired with a hidden rate category,
#           slow (S) or fast (F), giving four states 0S, 1S, 0F, 1F with
#               Q = [ Q_S - D_SF   D_SF      ]
#                   [ D_FS        Q_F - D_FS ]
#           (Eq. asr-hrm). Q_S and Q_F are symmetric 2x2 matrices with rates
#           r_slow < r_fast (ordered to avoid label switching) and D_SF = D_FS
#           = switch * I. Only the observed state is known at the tips.
#           Compared with a one-category Mk model by stepping-stone sampling.
# Book:     Chapter 12, "Heterogeneous and hidden-rate models" (#asr-hidden);
#           Chapter 7 (covarion models).
# Estimates: r_slow, r_fast, switch; log marginal likelihood of HRM vs Mk.
# Data:     data/traits/hrm.nex (40 independent binary features) on tree16.tre
# Run:      cd revbayes && rb analyses/traits/07_hidden_rates.Rev [--args n_gen]
# Runtime:  about 1 minute
################################################################################

seed(1107)
n_gen = 10000
if (args.size() > 1) n_gen = int(args[2])
n_cats  = 20
pp_gen  = 500
out_dir = "output/traits/07_hidden_rates/"
t_start = time("seconds")

# NB: every model gets its OWN copy of the tree (and of the root frequencies):
# model() collects every node connected to its argument, including through
# shared constant nodes, so models that share a tree object would be merged
# into one graph and their likelihoods added in the power posteriors.
tree_h <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
tree_m <- readTrees("data/traits/tree16.tre")[1]
feat <- readDiscreteCharacterData("data/traits/hrm.nex")
# expand: observed 0 -> {0S, 0F} (states 0, 2); observed 1 -> {1S, 1F} (states 1, 3)
feat_hidden <- feat.expandCharacters(2)

write("model,lnML_stepping_stone,lnML_path_sampling\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv")

############################ HRM
r_slow ~ dnExponential(1.0)
r_diff ~ dnExponential(1.0)
r_fast := r_slow + r_diff
switch ~ dnExponential(1.0)
mv_h = VectorMoves()
mv_h.append( mvScale(r_slow, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
mv_h.append( mvScale(r_diff, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
mv_h.append( mvScale(switch, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
# off-diagonal elements in row order (0S, 1S, 0F, 1F)
Q_h := fnFreeK([ r_slow, switch, 0.0,
                 r_slow, 0.0,    switch,
                 switch, 0.0,    r_fast,
                 0.0,    switch, r_fast ], rescaled = FALSE)
ctmc_h ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree_h, Q = Q_h, rootFrequencies = simplex(rep(1, 4)),
                     type = "NaturalNumbers", nSites = feat.nchar())
ctmc_h.clamp(feat_hidden)
mod_h = model(Q_h)
mn_h = VectorMonitors()
mn_h.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "HRM_model.log", printgen = 10) )
mn_h.append( mnScreen(printgen = 5000, r_slow, r_fast, switch) )
mcmc_h = mcmc(mod_h, mn_h, mv_h, nruns = 1)
mcmc_h.burnin(generations = 1000, tuningInterval = 100)
mcmc_h.run(generations = n_gen, tuningInterval = 0)
pp_h = powerPosterior(mod_h, mv_h, VectorMonitors(), out_dir + "HRM_powp.log", cats = n_cats, sampleFreq = 10)
pp_h.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
pp_h.run(generations = pp_gen)
ss = steppingStoneSampler(out_dir + "HRM_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
ps = pathSampler(out_dir + "HRM_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
write("HRM", ss, ps, filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE, separator = ",")
write("\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE)

############################ one-category Mk (symmetric)
q_mk ~ dnExponential(1.0)
mv_m = VectorMoves()
mv_m.append( mvScale(q_mk, lambda = 0.5, weight = 2.0) )
Q_m := fnFreeK([q_mk, q_mk], rescaled = FALSE)
ctmc_m ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree = tree_m, Q = Q_m, rootFrequencies = simplex([1, 1]),
                     type = "Standard", nSites = feat.nchar())
ctmc_m.clamp(feat)
mod_m = model(Q_m)
mn_m = VectorMonitors()
mn_m.append( mnModel(filename = out_dir + "MK_model.log", printgen = 10) )
mcmc_m = mcmc(mod_m, mn_m, mv_m, nruns = 1)
mcmc_m.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
mcmc_m.run(generations = 5000, tuningInterval = 0)
pp_m = powerPosterior(mod_m, mv_m, VectorMonitors(), out_dir + "MK_powp.log", cats = n_cats, sampleFreq = 10)
pp_m.burnin(generations = 500, tuningInterval = 100)
pp_m.run(generations = pp_gen)
ss = steppingStoneSampler(out_dir + "MK_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
ps = pathSampler(out_dir + "MK_powp.log", "power", "likelihood", "\t").marginal()
write("MK", ss, ps, filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE, separator = ",")
write("\n", filename = out_dir + "marginal_likelihoods.csv", append = TRUE)

write("runtime_s", time("seconds") - t_start, filename = out_dir + "runtime.txt", separator = "\t")
q()
